findings.what: The caption says the readings are 'worked out from each law and rounded', but the lamp's 98 and 45 lux were moved off the law on purpose (it gives 100 and 44.4), and screens 11 and 14 teach from that miss as if it were real scatter; the caption should say these are example readings and that two lamp readings were moved to show scatter, as the lesson's 'ignores' note already does.

findings.where: Explain text, lamp paragraph (and the 'ignores' note on long fittings)
findings.what: 'the inverse-square law textbooks give for a small lamp' and 'near a long fitting the light falls off more slowly' are physics claims with none of the lesson's four sources behind them; cite a source or label them as unsourced.

ln(10 e^(−t/47)) = ln 10 − t/47 skips the middle step (product law, then 'ln of e to a power is the power') that screen 3 spells out line by line for the gas; add that line so the capacitor's straight form is earned the same way.

The lesson says the log-linear gradient is log b but no screen turns a gradient back into b (10^gradient), so 'convert back' is only ever practised on intercepts; screen 12's 3 × 2ˣ card could ask for b (10^0.301 = 2).

'A log axis has no 0 ... so the upright axis sits at log V = 0' gives the drawing as the reason; the real reason the crossing is log C is that the −n log V term is zero at log V = 0, and a graph whose axis starts elsewhere has to be extended to log x = 0 (or c worked out as y − mx).

It ends with the x switch on, so the picture left is bent and the readouts say 'not straight' while 'RC ≈ 1 ÷ 0.0212 ≈ 47 s' still shows beneath; flip x back off at the end, or dim the forms while the line is gone.

The line misses 98 lux by about half a pixel, so it looks as if it goes through the reading and he has to take 'misses a little' on trust; show what the line reads at 2 m (100 lux) beside the 98 reading before he answers.
The shrinking-gap bars are amber (fill2 with an amber outline), but amber means key terms or what is due, and the brief asks for the gap in ink, as in lesson 3.

findings.where: Screen 7, y-axis title at the end
findings.what: Once the voltage dots become gap dots, the axis still says 'voltage (V)'; the next screen calls the same axis 'gap, 10 − v (V)', so the title could change as the gaps drop.

Each paragraph runs 13 to 16 lines, so on a phone the graph sits at or below the fold and the 3 to 4.5 s demonstration is over before he scrolls to it; Play again rescues it, but shorter text, or starting the motion when the graph comes into view, would let him see it the first time.

findings.where: Screen 1 text and screen 14's third answer at 360 px
findings.what: 'y-axis' breaks across lines at its hyphen ('y-' / 'axis') in the paragraph, and 'inverse-' / 'square' does the same on the answer button; use a non-breaking hyphen.
About 100 px of empty space sits between the graph and the answer buttons, pushing the answers away from the picture they ask about (and below the fold on a phone).
